contract.credential: the module pod's projected ServiceAccount token, minted for the audience accounts and re-read from its projection before every mint
checks: TokenReview with the audience accounts: a token for any other audience, cluster or an expired one is refused
the token was projected for at most 600 seconds (its iat and exp, read after TokenReview authenticated it)
the token's ServiceAccount and namespace identify exactly one declared principal, and it is the one asked for
the pod the TOKEN names is read: its live UID equals the token's, it is Running and not being deleted
the declared container is a regular container in state running, and its RUNNING image (status imageID, never the spec's image) equals the build the principal's authority document approves

no other container may run in the pod: no other regular container, no init container still running or restartable, and no ephemeral container in any state; init containers that completed are tolerated and never supply the digest

refusals.verdict: the token is refused, belongs to another workload, or the pod runs an unapproved build: nothing is minted, and the caller is not told which check failed
refusals.unbound: the host could not establish the execution (API server unreachable, no execution binding wired, the pod or container not started yet, no image id): nothing is minted, and the answer is retryable

rules: No secret proves a module's identity. MODULE_IDENTITY_SECRETS, MODULE_REGISTRATION_SECRETS and SOLUTION_REGISTRATION_SECRETS are deleted, with both registration mints.
Execution binding is wired only with delivered authority; a host with no delivery mints for no module.
Every mint record names the execution it was bound to: namespace, ServiceAccount, pod, pod UID, container, running image and approved incarnation.
contract.limitation: The Work Context does not yet SEAL the installation id and revision: the host signs the sdk-go encoding, which carries no seal, and module principals hold no installation until #1057. The execution is bound at mint and recorded, not sealed.

replay.closed: a token from another workload, audience or cluster; a replaced pod; an unapproved build or container; a stopped container or terminating pod; a token older than 600 seconds
replay.residual: the projected token is a bearer credential: a peer holding a copied, still-valid token of an approved running pod and the broker's perimeter credential can mint as that pod's principal until the token expires
replay.closingOption: request-origin identity: the mesh's pod-specific mTLS identity of the connection, conveyed by the broker and required to name the reviewed pod UID — an owner decision, not built

contract.scope: Every request proxied to a catalog route or a declared solution upstream.
contract.check: The gateway runs an ext_authz Check and proxies only on success. A registered target never changes which check runs.
contract.inboundHeaders: Every canonical identity header is stripped from the inbound request before the verified principal is stamped, so a caller cannot present one on a route that stamps a subset.
rules: An upstream reads identity only from these headers; it never re-derives identity from a forwarded bearer.
x-credential-kind names what the perimeter authenticated, a fact only the perimeter holds.
An upstream that trusts an unstamped header trusts caller-supplied input.

contract.principle: Every declared requirement is checked before activation, so an incompatible remote is never handed to a browser. A declared requirement the host does not check is not a compatibility contract.

manifestFields.checkedAgainst: the versions the host publishes into the sealed scope

contract.absentMajorDefault: An undeclared major defaults to 1, the major in force when the field was introduced, and never to the host's current major, which would make every silent manifest compatible by definition at exactly the upgrade this check exists for.
contract.rangeGrammar: A deliberately small semver subset: || alternatives of space-separated ^ ~ >= > <= < =, a bare version, or *. A range outside the grammar is refused, never approximated.

sharedScope.ownedByHost: The host owns the single React instance and publishes exact versions into the Module-Federation shared scope; a remote declares the range it needs of each.
sharedScope.versions: The exact published version of each key is a release fact of the host build, carried by the module package rather than restated here.

refusal.whole: An incompatible stored manifest is omitted from every frontend projection.
refusal.unavailable: A failed registry refresh drops the cached snapshot and the read fails closed. No stale manifest is served.

headers.Authorization: Bearer <the module pod's projected ServiceAccount token>

broker.authorizedAgainst: the projected token, bound by BindExecution to the principal's declared workload and approved build

rules: The pod's projected token is the only credential; no secret substitutes for it and the gateway forwards it unread.
accounts owns every rule about what the resulting capability may do. The gateway mints nothing and adds no authority of its own.

headers.Authorization: Bearer <the module pod's projected ServiceAccount token>

refusals.401: the module is not proven: internal token, projected token, workload, running build, or module declaration
refusals.403: the proven module's binding is undeclared or declares no headless_scopes
refusals.503: the host could not establish the caller's execution; nothing was decided and the module retries

broker.authorizedAgainst: the projected token, bound by BindExecution to the principal's declared workload and approved build

token.tenant: the tenant MODULE_PRINCIPALS declares for the module
token.authorizationRevision: a non-zero digest of the module's MODULE_PRINCIPALS entry; CheckAuthorizationRevision confirms it against the current entry and answers PermissionDenied on any mismatch

rules: A binding without headless_scopes cannot be minted with no person present; invoke_scopes are never reused implicitly.
headless_scopes must be a subset of the binding's invoke_scopes.
The caller names only the binding. Audience, scopes, tenant, actor and lifetime are deployment policy.
The gateway mints nothing and adds no authority of its own.

contract.separation: Deployment registration, per-organization installation, and entitlement are three different things.

registration.governs: whether /s/{id} renders a remote and whether /solutions/{id}/... proxies

composes: a least-privilege standing grant with an audience and scope ceiling
installation.uninstall: Removes the agent's standing grant and revokes the agent principal, then marks the installation revoked. It does NOT reverse the whole composition: the scope node is retained so a reinstall reuses it, and durable subscriptions are not deleted. Revoking the agent principal is what withdraws the authority.
installation.subscriptions: The solution's declared consumes are materialized into durable subscriptions for the new agent principal AFTER the install transaction commits, not as part of the composition. The write is idempotent and best-effort: a failure is logged and the install still succeeds, to be recovered by a reinstall or a runtime Subscribe. A solution that consumes nothing materializes nothing.

entitlement.governs: feature availability within the product, independently of the other two

contract.limitation: Uninstalling in one organization revokes that organization's agent authority and does not remove the solution's nav entry, page, or gateway route, for that organization or any other. A registered solution's UI and API surface is visible to every tenant of the deployment. Per-tenant admission before route or page exposure is an additional gate that is not implemented here.

contract.authority: Delivery declares presence through SolutionHostBinding; accounts reconciles the durable registry.

frontendNavigation.authorization: viewer entitlements joined by immutable target id

contract.routing: Catalog routes own module REST paths. Solution routes resolve the declared target and upstream together before per-viewer installation admission. Unknown routes return 404.
